mainTopic: The end of the story of שילא and רב אסי; whether קושי blood or a birth cancels a זבה's seven clean days, and whether the birth days count toward them
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of שילא and רב אסי. שילא dies right after רב אסי, and a flying myrtle at the funeral shows the two have made peace. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה's topic of blood from קושי (labor pains). רבא asks whether such blood cancels a זבה's count of seven clean days. The question is whether cancelling depends on making her impure or on being able to cause זיבה. After a back-and-forth about a זב whose discharge came by אונס, the גמרא concludes that for רבי אליעזר even a discharge that cannot cause זיבה cancels the count, but for the רבנן it does not. אביי rules that קושי blood does not cancel the count. Next, רבי מרינוס teaches that a birth does not cancel the count either. אביי and רבא then argue whether the birth days themselves count toward the seven clean days, and רבא brings two proofs that אביי pushes away. The amud ends in the middle of אביי's explanation of why the תורה needed separate פסוקים for a זב and a זבה, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שילא prepares for his own death
steps.stepSummary: After רב אסי dies, שילא tells his wife to prepare his burial shrouds, and then he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: שילא went and said to his wife: Prepare provisions (burial shrouds) for me, so that רב אסי will not go and tell רב bad things about me. She prepared them, and שילא died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a story from just before this section. שילא feels responsible for רב אסי's death and expects to die soon himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שילא wants to follow רב אסי quickly to the next world. That way רב אסי cannot complain about him to רב without שילא being there too. His wife prepares the shrouds, and שילא dies right afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Provisions for a journey; here, burial shrouds
His wife (literally 'his household')
He passed away (literally 'his soul rested')
Things against me; complaints about me

phrases.english: Sheila went and said to his wife:
Prepare provisions for me
phrases.notes: "Provisions" here means burial shrouds, packing for the trip to the next world.

phrases.english: so that he will not go and tell Rav
phrases.notes: "He" is רב אסי, who had just died.

phrases.english: things against me.
She prepared the provisions for him.
Sheila passed away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב אסי and שילא from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שילא prepared for death so that he would not be blamed in the next world without being present, and he died right afterward.

steps.title: The flying myrtle shows the two made peace
steps.stepSummary: At the funeral, the myrtle flies from one bier to the other, and people understand that the two חכמים have made peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: They saw that the myrtle was flying from this bier to that bier. They said: Learn from this that the חכמים have made peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a sign. The myrtle placed on the biers jumps between the two biers, and the people take it to mean that רב אסי and שילא have made up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, there was a fight between them. The myrtle passing back and forth shows that the fight is over and they are now friends in the next world. The phrase שמע מינה tells us this is the conclusion people drew from the sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Myrtle, which was placed on a bier
Bier (also means bed)
Reconciliation; making peace
Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רב אסי and שילא ends peacefully: the flying myrtle shows they made up after death.

phrases.english: They saw that the myrtle was flying
from this bier to that bier.
They said: Learn from this
the Sages have made peace.
phrases.notes: "The Sages" here means רב אסי and שילא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנַן פְּיָיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 1 with a closing sign.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אסי and שילא made peace after their deaths.

steps.title: Does labor-pain blood cancel a זבה's clean count?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether blood that comes out because of קושי cancels the seven clean days of a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Blood from labor pains, does it cancel the count in זיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's topic, blood from קושי. רבא asks a new question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זבה must count seven clean days. Normally, if she sees blood during them, she has to start counting again (סותר). The משנה said קושי blood does not make a woman a זבה. רבא asks whether it can still cancel a count she has already started.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question that has no clear answer
Labor pains before birth that cause bleeding
Cancels the count, so she must start the seven clean days again
The status of a זבה (blood outside the regular time of נדה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two questions. The משנה already said קושי blood does not MAKE a woman a זבה. רבא is asking something new: whether it CANCELS a count that a woman who is already a זבה has started.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
Labor pains: what is the law
that it should cancel the count in ziva?
phrases.notes: The count meant here is the seven clean days a זבה has to count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to the halachic topic of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood from קושי cancels a זבה's count of seven clean days.

steps.title: The two ways to look at the question
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the two sides: maybe anything that makes a woman impure cancels the count, or maybe only something that causes זיבה cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it anything that makes a woman impure that cancels? This blood also makes her impure, like the days of נדה. Or maybe only something that causes זיבה cancels, and this blood does not cause זיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why his question is hard by giving the two possible reasons for the rule of cancelling. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: what cancels the count is impurity. קושי blood is impure (like נדה blood), so it would cancel. Side two: only blood that could make her a זבה cancels the count. קושי blood cannot do that, so it would not cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that makes a person impure
Something that causes (here, causes זיבה status)
Or perhaps; brings in the other side of the question
The days when blood makes a woman a נדה

phrases.english: Is it something that makes impure that cancels,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי נָמֵי מְטַמֵּא כִּימֵי נִדָּה הוּא,
phrases.english: and this too makes impure, like the days of niddah,
or perhaps something that causes cancels,
phrases.notes: "Causes" means causes her to become a זבה.

phrases.english: and this does not cause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of רבא's question from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the rule of cancelling based on impurity, or on the ability to cause זיבה?

steps.title: אביי proves it from a discharge caused by outside factors
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that something can cancel the count even though it does not cause זיבה: a זב's discharge that comes by אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: A discharge by אונס in זיבה proves it. It does not cause זיבה, and still it cancels the count!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבא with a proof from a similar case. A discharge that comes by אונס cannot make someone a זב, but it still cancels the clean count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This knocks out the second side of רבא's question, that only something which causes זיבה can cancel. The אונס case shows that something can cancel without causing זיבה. So קושי blood, which is impure even though it does not cause זיבה, should also cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: A discharge brought on by an outside cause, not by the body itself
Will prove; a case brought as proof
That does not cause (זיבה)

steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's proof suggests that the rule of cancelling depends on impurity, not on causing זיבה. That would mean קושי blood cancels a זבה's count.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
A discharge by force in ziva will prove it,
phrases.notes: This is a זב whose discharge came from an outside cause, not from his own body.

phrases.english: for it does not cause, and yet it cancels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question by knocking out the second side in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That something can cancel the count of clean days even if it does not cause זיבה, so קושי blood should cancel.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of a זב's discharge by אונס: it does not make him a זב, but it cancels his seven clean days.

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof: an אונס discharge can also cause זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the proof fails, because a זב's discharge through אונס can also make a person a זב, as the משנה shows for the third sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: No. This also causes זיבה. As we learned: if a man saw a first sighting, we check him. After a second sighting, we check him. After a third sighting, we do not check him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away אביי's proof. He says a discharge through אונס is not a clear example of something that cancels the count without causing זיבה, because it sometimes does cause זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי wanted to show that something can cancel the count without making a person a זב. רבא answers from the משנה: at the third sighting we do not check for אונס at all, so even an אונס discharge counts toward making him a זב. That means an אונס discharge can be a 'causer' (גורם), and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No, that is not so
Something that causes a person to become a זב
A sighting, meaning one discharge of זיבה
We check him, to see whether the discharge came from an outside cause (אונס)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Checking' here does not mean checking whether he is pure or impure in general. It means checking whether the discharge came through אונס, like illness or overeating. If it did, the discharge does not count toward his becoming a זב.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering אביי's proof from the step before.

phrases.english: this too is something that causes [him to be a זב],
as we learned in a משנה:
If he saw a first sighting,
we check him;
after the second, we check him;
after the third, we do not check him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאיֵי, הַאי נָמֵי גּוֹרֵם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from the אונס discharge of a זב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from a זב's אונס discharge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An אונס discharge is not truly 'non-causing', because at the third sighting it does make a person a זב.

steps.title: אביי asks about רבי אליעזר, who checks even the third sighting
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: according to רבי אליעזר, an אונס discharge never causes זיבה, so would it then also not cancel the count?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר, who said that even after the third sighting we check him, would you really say that since it does not cause זיבה, it does not cancel the count?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer by pointing to רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer only works for the view that the third sighting is not checked. רבי אליעזר checks even the third, so for him an אונס discharge never causes זיבה. אביי asks whether רבא really accepts that, for רבי אליעזר, such a discharge does not cancel the clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels, undoes the count of clean days
Since, because
Even at the third sighting

phrases.english: And according to רבי אליעזר, who said:
Even after the third we check him,
would you really say that since it does not cause [זיבה],
it does not cancel [the count]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר: אַף בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer by applying it to רבי אליעזר's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that an אונס discharge cancels the count only because it can cause זיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי אליעזר an אונס discharge never causes זיבה, so by רבא's logic it should never cancel the count, which seems hard to accept.

steps.title: רבא accepts it: for רבי אליעזר, it does not cancel
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that yes, according to רבי אליעזר, an אונס discharge does not cancel the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to רבי אליעזר, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not back down. He agrees that according to רבי אליעזר, an אונס discharge does not cancel the clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of looking for a way out, רבא simply accepts the result. His rule stays the same: only something that can cause זיבה cancels the count. For רבי אליעזר, an אונס discharge never causes זיבה, so it does not cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָכִי נָמֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: According to רבי אליעזר, that is indeed so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by accepting its conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the result of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed hard to say that an אונס discharge would not cancel the count.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, an אונס discharge really does not cancel the count.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר seems to show that אונס does cancel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's ruling that after the fourth sighting we do not check, and suggests this is about cancelling the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says: Even after the third sighting we check him; after the fourth we do not check him. Is this not about cancelling the count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading of רבי אליעזר with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says no check is needed after the fourth sighting. The גמרא suggests the reason is that even an אונס fourth sighting cancels his clean days, so there is nothing to check. That would mean that for רבי אליעזר an אונס discharge does cancel the count, which goes against what רבא just said.

keyTerms.meaning: At the fourth sighting
Is it not that...? (a suggested reading)
Cancelling the count of clean days

phrases.english: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says,
Even after the third we check him;
after the fourth we do not check him.
Is it not about cancelling [the count]?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַף בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 8 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that for רבי אליעזר an אונס discharge does not cancel the count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule of 'no check at the fourth' is about cancelling the count, then רבי אליעזר holds that אונס does cancel.

steps.title: No, the fourth sighting is about impurity through carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the fourth-sighting rule is about making that drop impure through משא, not about cancelling the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about making that drop impure through carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge and protects רבא's reading of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא can be read differently. 'No check at the fourth' means that drop is impure and makes something impure through carrying (משא), even if it came through אונס. It says nothing about cancelling the clean days, so רבא's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it impure
A drop, here the drop of זיבה
Carrying, a way that impurity passes on when someone carries the impure thing

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רבא's reading survives: the ברייתא's 'no check at the fourth' can be about the drop's impurity through משא, not about cancelling the count. The next step brings a ברייתא that overturns this reading.

phrases.english: No, it is about making that drop impure through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא offered in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא is about cancelling the count.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be about the drop's impurity through משא, not about סתירה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר says the checking is only for the offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר saying the checks are for the קרבן and not for cancelling the count. That means even an אונס discharge cancels the count, which goes against רבא's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: at the third sighting, רבי אליעזר says we check him. At the fourth sighting we do not check him. 'I said this for the offering, not for cancelling the count.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא where רבי אליעזר explains his own rule. He says the checking only matters for the קרבן, not for cancelling the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the fourth-sighting rule was pushed off as being about טומאת משא. Now רבי אליעזר says outright that the checking is not about סתירה. So even an אונס discharge must cancel the count, which goes against רבא's answer in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: We check: we ask whether the discharge came from an outside cause, such as food or strain
The offering a full זב brings after he becomes pure
Cancelling: wiping out the clean days already counted
The fourth sighting of discharge

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 9. There the rule was only 'we do not check at the fourth,' and it could be pushed off. Here רבי אליעזר adds his own reason, 'לקרבן אמרתי ולא לסתירה,' and that reason closes off the step 10 answer.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
At the third sighting, Rabbi Eliezer says
we check him;
at the fourth we do not check him.
I said it for the offering,
and not for cancelling the count.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge of step 9 with clearer wording, so the step 10 answer no longer works.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 8) that for רבי אליעזר an אונס discharge does not cancel the count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the checks are only for the קרבן and not for סתירה, then סתירה happens without any checking. So even an אונס discharge cancels the count.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's view is settled; what do the רבנן hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that for רבי אליעזר even a discharge that does not cause זיבה cancels the count. It now asks what the רבנן hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for רבי אליעזר we can settle it: something that does not cause זיבה still cancels the count. But what do the רבנן hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives in on רבי אליעזר's view and opens a new question about the רבנן. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original question was whether a 'דבר שאינו גורם' cancels the count. The ברייתא answered it for רבי אליעזר, so the question now moves to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Settle it, resolve the question
A discharge that cannot cause someone to become a זב
Cancels the clean days already counted
The Sages who disagree with רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi Eliezer,
settle it: something that does not cause זיבה does cancel;
according to the Rabbis, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 11 and moves the open question over to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, for the רבנן, a discharge that cannot cause זיבה cancels the count of clean days

steps.title: The teaching of רבי אבין's father: what it causes, it cancels
steps.stepSummary: The father of רבי אבין teaches that זיבה cancels seven days because it 'caused' seven, and קרי cancels one day because it 'caused' one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what the father of רבי אבין taught: what did his זיבה cause him? Seven days. So it cancels seven. What did his קרי cause him? One day. So it cancels one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that matches how much a discharge cancels to how much it 'caused.' This is the source it will use to answer the question about the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching explains why זיבה wipes out all seven clean days while קרי wipes out only one. The key word is 'גרם' (caused), and the next step will look closely at that word.

keyTerms.meaning: Caused
His זיבה discharge
His seminal emission
Therefore

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין:
phrases.english: Come and hear what the father of Rabbi Avin taught:
What did his זיבה cause him? Seven days.
Therefore it cancels seven.

phrases.aramaic: מָה גָּרַם לוֹ קִרְיוֹ — יוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: What did his emission cause him? One day.
phrases.notes: A זב who has a seminal emission during his clean days loses only that one day, not the whole count.

phrases.english: Therefore it cancels one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question about the רבנן asked in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That for the רבנן a discharge that does not cause זיבה does not cancel the count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the father of רבי אבין

steps.title: Reading the word 'caused' closely
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'seven' means. If it only meant seven days of טומאה, he should have said 'טמא שבעה.' So the word 'caused' must mean that only a discharge that causes זיבה cancels the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'seven' mean? If you say it makes him impure for seven days, he should have said 'just as his זיבה makes him impure for seven.' So is it not saying: something that causes זיבה cancels, and something that does not cause it does not cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at why the teacher said 'caused' instead of 'made impure.' It pulls the proof out of that choice of word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point were only how long the טומאה lasts, the plain word 'טמא' would be enough. Choosing 'גרם' shows that cancelling depends on the discharge being able to cause זיבה. So קושי blood, which cannot cause זיבה, does not cancel the count according to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that is about to be rejected)
Makes him impure
He should have said
Is it not rather that... (introduces the real meaning)

phrases.english: What does 'seven' mean?
If you say that it makes him impure for seven days,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״מָה זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא שִׁבְעָה״ מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: then he should have said 'just as his זיבה makes him impure for seven,'
So is it not that something that causes zivah cancels,
and something that does not cause it does not cancel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the teaching from step 13 to pull out the proof.
steps.raayaObject: For the רבנן, a דבר שאינו גורם does not cancel the count
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'גרם' in the teaching of the father of רבי אבין

steps.title: Conclusion: for the רבנן it does not cancel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof. For the רבנן, a discharge that cannot cause זיבה does not cancel the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question: the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the two views split. For רבי אליעזר even an אונס discharge cancels the count. For the רבנן only a discharge that can cause זיבה cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: even a discharge that cannot cause זיבה (אונס) cancels the count. רבנן: only a discharge that can cause זיבה cancels it ('דבר הגורם סותר').

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reading from step 14 as the answer to step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the רבנן, a discharge that does not cause זיבה does not cancel the count of clean days.

steps.title: אביי's rule: labor-pain blood does not cancel the count
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the practical rule that blood from קושי does not cancel a זבה's count. Any תנא who says it does follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that labor-pain blood does not cancel the count of זיבה. If you find a תנא who says it does cancel, that is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proof in step 15, אביי turns the conclusion into a clear practical rule about קושי blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that comes with labor pains cannot cause זיבה. So according to the רבנן of step 15, it does not cancel the seven clean days. Only רבי אליעזר, who holds that even a discharge that cannot cause זיבה cancels the count, would say otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / we have a tradition
Labor pains (blood that comes out with them)
Cancels (the seven clean days already counted)
The status of a זבה, who must count seven clean days
A sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows the רבנן: קושי blood does not cancel a זבה's count. The opposite view belongs to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion about which discharges cancel the count and gives the practical halacha.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition,
labor-pain blood does not cancel the count of zivah.
And if you find a tanna who says it does cancel —
that is Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 15 to קושי blood as practical halacha.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קושי blood does not cancel a זבה's count, following the רבנן. Only רבי אליעזר disagrees.

steps.title: רבי מרינוס: a birth does not cancel the count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מרינוס: if a זבה gives birth during her seven clean days, the birth does not cancel her count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught that רבי מרינוס says: A birth does not cancel the count of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about a related case: a זבה who gives birth in the middle of her seven clean days. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving birth makes a woman טמאה with טומאת לידה. Even so, רבי מרינוס rules that the birth does not wipe out the clean days she already counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving birth (brings its own kind of טומאה)
Cancels (feminine form of סותר)

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Marinus says:
Birth does not cancel the count of zivah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קושי blood to a related case, the birth itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A birth during the seven clean days does not cancel the days already counted.

steps.title: Do the birth days count toward the seven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the days of birth-טומאה can themselves be counted as part of the seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Do those days count toward the seven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question on רבי מרינוס. It is setting up a disagreement between אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know the birth does not erase the earlier days. The new question is whether the birth days are counted as clean days, or whether she must count around them.

keyTerms.meaning: Do they count toward the total? (literally, 'go up')

phrases.english: A question was raised: may they count?
phrases.notes: He means the days of birth-טומאה. Do they count as part of her seven clean days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question on רבי מרינוס's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the days of birth-טומאה count toward the seven clean days.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the birth days do not cancel and do not count. רבא says they do not cancel and they do count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It does not cancel and does not count. רבא said: It does not cancel, and it does count.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the earlier days are not erased. According to אביי, the birth days are like a pause, and she continues counting after them. According to רבא, the birth days themselves are counted as part of the seven.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not count toward the total
It counts toward the total

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֵינָהּ סוֹתֶרֶת וְאֵינָהּ עוֹלָה.
phrases.english: Abaye said: It does not cancel, and it does not count.
Rava said: It does not cancel, and it does count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אביי אמר אינה סותרת ואינה עולה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: the birth days do not count. רבא: the birth days do count.

steps.title: רבא's source: 'and after, she will be pure'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק 'ואחר תטהר'. It teaches that no טומאה may separate between the seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? As it is taught: 'And after, she will be pure.' 'After' means after all of them, so that no טומאה separates between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to prove his opinion by quoting a ברייתא about the פסוק of the seven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'after' as 'after all seven days together.' That means the seven days must be connected, with no טומאה breaking them up.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
'And after, she will be pure' (the פסוק of the seven days)
Separates / interrupts

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it is taught: "And after, she will be pure" —
"after" means after all of them,
so that no impurity separates between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא brings a source for his opinion from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the birth days count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'ואחר תטהר': no טומאה may separate between the seven days.

steps.title: רבא's proof: otherwise the birth would separate
steps.stepSummary: If the birth days count, the seven days stay connected. If they do not count, the birth separates the days, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the birth days count, that fits 'no טומאה separates.' But if you say they do not count, then the birth separates them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the ברייתא proves his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אביי's view, the birth days sit in the middle of the count without being part of it. That leaves a gap of טומאה between the clean days. Since the ברייתא says no טומאה may separate them, the birth days must count.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this fits well)
It separates

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it counts —
that is why the impurity does not separate,
but if you say it does not count —
the birth separates them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא of step 20 supports רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That the birth days count toward the seven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Only if they count is there no טומאה separating the days, as the ברייתא requires.

steps.title: אביי: only זיבה-טומאה may not separate
steps.stepSummary: אביי can answer that the ברייתא only forbids a טומאה of זיבה from separating the days. A birth's טומאה is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי can tell you: it means that no טומאה of זיבה separates between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how אביי would push away רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads the word 'טומאה' in the ברייתא narrowly, as only the טומאה of זיבה. Birth-טומאה is a different kind, so it may sit between the days without breaking them up. That way the birth days do not count, but they also do not cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: The טומאה that comes from a discharge of זיבה

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: birth does not cancel and does not count. רבא: birth does not cancel and does count. רבא's proof from 'ואחר תטהר' is pushed away, because אביי reads it as only about טומאת זיבה.

phrases.english: And Abaye can say to you:
that there should not be an impurity of zivah
separating between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from steps 20 and 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבא's opinion itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed 'טומאה' means any טומאה. It can be read as only טומאת זיבה.

steps.title: רבא's second proof: 'from her זיבה and not from her birth'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא on the word מזובה. It teaches that a זבה counts her seven days even during צרעת and even during birth days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: 'From her זיבה.' This means from her זיבה and not from her leprosy, and from her זיבה and not from her giving birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new proof that the days of birth-טומאה can count as part of the seven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says she counts seven days once she is clean 'from her זיבה.' The ברייתא learns that only the זיבה has to stop. Other טומאות, like צרעת or birth, do not stop her from counting, so birth days can be part of the seven days, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: From her זיבה (ויקרא 15:28)
Her נגע, meaning her צרעת
Her giving birth, meaning the birth-טומאה

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught: 'From her ziva'
from her ziva, and not from her leprosy,
from her ziva, and not from her giving birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first proof was pushed off in step 22, רבא brings a second proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that birth days count toward the seven clean days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'מזובה' (ויקרא 15:28): 'and not from her birth'.

steps.title: אביי removes 'and not from her birth' from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא should only teach the צרעת rule. The words about birth should be taken out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי could say to you: Teach only one thing, 'from her זיבה and not from her leprosy.' Do not teach 'and not from her giving birth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רבא's proof by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי keeps the part about צרעת but takes out the part about birth. Without that line, the ברייתא gives no proof that birth days count, so אביי's view can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: One (only one teaching)
And do not teach (take this line out)

phrases.english: And Abaye could say to you:
Teach one: 'from her ziva and not from her leprosy,'
and do not teach 'and not from her giving birth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's proof in step 23 by changing the wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the line about birth in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof rests on words that אביי says should not be in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: without 'birth', the leprosy line teaches nothing new
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the birth line must stay. If the ברייתא only taught the צרעת rule, it would be pointless, because the פסוק about a זב already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא: What is this? It works fine if you say 'from her זיבה and not from her birth.' Since he needed to teach birth, he also taught leprosy along with it. But if you say only 'from her זיבה and not from her leprosy,' that is already learned from 'And when the זב is purified from his זיבה': from his זיבה and not from his leprosy!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's new wording. He shows that without the birth line, the ברייתא repeats something we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is mainly about birth, it makes sense that it adds צרעת along with it. But the צרעת rule alone is already learned from the זב פסוק (ויקרא 15:13). So the ברייתא's real new lesson must be about birth, and that supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a sharp pushback)
It works out fine if
Since (he taught one thing, he added another with it)
Because of, along with
It is learned from
A man with a זיבה discharge

phrases.english: And Rava: What is this?
Granted, if you say 'from her ziva and not from her giving birth,'
since he needed to teach birth,
he taught her leprosy along with birth.
But if you say 'from her ziva and not from her leprosy,'

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מִ״וְּכִי יִטְהַר הַזָּב מִזּוֹבוֹ״ נָפְקָא
phrases.english: this is learned from 'And when the zav is purified from his ziva,'
'from his ziva' and not from his leprosy!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא, הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's proof by attacking אביי's wording from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's wording that keeps only 'and not from her leprosy'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With that wording, the ברייתא teaches nothing new, because the זב פסוק already teaches the צרעת rule.

steps.title: אביי: one פסוק for a זב, one for a זבה, and both are needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the two פסוקים are not repeats. One is about a זב and one is about a זבה, and the גמרא begins to show why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי: One פסוק is about a זב, and one is about a זבה. And both are needed, because if the Merciful One had written...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows why the צרעת line is not extra. The גמרא then starts a new explanation, which continues in the next part, of why the תורה needed to say it twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the צרעת rule for a זבה was already known from the זב. אביי answers that we could not have learned a זבה from a זב, so each פסוק is needed. That means the ברייתא can teach only the צרעת rule, as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman with a זיבה flow
And both are needed
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence 'if the Merciful One had written' is not finished here. The reason why both פסוקים are needed comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: And Abaye would answer:
One is about a zav, and one is about a zava.
phrases.notes: 'From his ziva' (ויקרא 15:13) is about the man; 'from her ziva' (ויקרא 15:28) is about the woman.

phrases.english: And both are needed, because if the Merciful One had written

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two פסוקים are about different people (זב and זבה), and both are needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The זבה פסוק seemed to repeat the זב פסוק about צרעת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק teaches its own case, so the ברייתא can teach only the צרעת rule without mentioning birth.
